page.layout: Running head top left, page number top right (plus a section page "71" in the head). One column of running text. A marginal note on the right beside the second paragraph (conclusio), and a second marginal note on the right beside the drop-cap paragraph below the chapter heading. Below the chapter heading: a title in italics, then the text starting with a woodcut initial.

p.i: anguine, utpote agni immaculati & incontaminati Christi.

main_text.p: Non igitur integra Servandi nos ratio consistit in eo, quod Christus JesusConclusio huius insufficientia demonstratur. veniens in mundum annuntiarit nobis salutis viam, eamq; in sua ipsius persona nobis ostenderit, sanctè scilicet Vivendo, Patiendo, Moriendo, & ex mortuis Resurgendo; quodq; olim in novissimo ille die sit venturus judicatum hominibus & credentibus sibiq; obedientibus datum vitam æternam: Proin-de hæc servandi ratio Christi MERITO ET SATISFACTIONE truncata, rectè insufficiens esse concluditur.
main_text.head: CAPUT IV.

head.i: ASSERTIO ET DEMON-stratio Meriti & Satisfactionis Servatoris Christi, ex eo, quod ipse Mediator, Reconciliator et Redem-tor noster fit.

page.notes: The page number "71" printed at the head (between the running head and the folio) is a section page number; only 253 was taken as page_number. The woodcut initial is a decorated Q whose letter is not clearly legible; read as Q[?]. "anguine" is the first word of the continued line and is partly obscured; the first letter may be an s. Marginal note texts are set in italic and in small type; their line breaks are not reproduced. "arcteq;" is read as printed with the abbreviation mark; a macron may be present. Long s was normalised to s. Printed hyphens kept at line ends ("Proin-de", "DEMON-stratio", "Redem-tor", "te-neo"). Page ends mid-word with "propri-" continuing on the next page.
